audit.why: The packet flags the chart as contradicting the 57.49% win rate because Sion holds 5 of 7 stages. I did NOT flip any row. This page is explicit and internally consistent about why: content.late states outright that 'your 57% win rate comes from what you do after lane, not from winning it' — Swain loses the 1v1 to a Heartsteel Sion and wins the game on teamfight drain, roaming fragments and objective timing. Every Sion row has a real argument behind it in the adjacent whys. Flipping rows to satisfy the win rate would invent a power shift the matchup does not have.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike names Unstoppable Onslaught with no cooldown and treats it purely as a damage threat.
audit.why: Unstoppable Onslaught is 140/100/60 — a 140s rank-1 cooldown is a long, countable window — and its real danger to Swain is the terrain flag: it creates a wall that cuts a retreat, and Swain has no dash. The _missing-interactions entry for this matchup says it directly: 'Sion can cut your retreat with Unstoppable Onslaught (R) and you have no dash — hold Flash for the wall, not the damage.'
audit.corrected: 140s at rank 1; hold Flash for the terrain, not the knockup, and root him before he accumulates charge distance.

audit.whatIsWrong: Roar of the Slayer is described as shredding shields in two places — whys[2] 'Roar of the Slayer shreds your shields' and wants.foe[1] 'shred his shield stacking' — and in content.mid as shredding 'your max HP scaling'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Sion fires a short range shockwave that damages and slows and reduces the Armor of the first enemy hit. If the shockwave hits a minion or monster, it will be knocked back, damaging, slowing, and reducing the Armor of all enemies that it passes through.' It shreds armour, not shields, and Swain has no shields and no max-HP scaling for it to touch. What it actually does in this matchup is slow you from 800 range and set up the charged Decimating Smash — and the minion-punt is a second way it reaches you through the wave. Naming the wrong effect hides the only part that matters.
audit.corrected: Roar of the Slayer slows and shreds armour from 800, and can knock a minion through you — it is the setup for the charged Q, not a shield-breaker.

audit.whatIsWrong: Glory in Death is called 'zombie passive' with no mention that its attacks heal him, and nothing on the page ties that to Grievous Wounds timing.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'After being killed, Sion will temporarily reanimate with rapidly decaying Health. His attacks become very rapid, heal him, and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health.' Against Swain that is doubly bad — the bonus damage scales on YOUR maximum health, which is the stat Ravenous Flock spends the whole game stacking. The _missing-interactions entry flags the anti-heal need. The itemization block already lists Oblivion Orb, but no field says why or when.
audit.corrected: Have Grievous Wounds before the kill, and remember his reanimated attacks scale on your max health — the fragment stack is a liability in that window.

audit.why: All four packet suspectNames are false positives: 'Sion's Unstoppable Onslaught', 'Use Unstoppable Onslaught', 'His Soul Furnace' and "Demonic Ascension's" are all correct names, flagged only by edit distance against the lowercased canonical strings.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are Sion's clearest ownership window and you have to survive them, not win them. His Soul Furnace shield regenerates every few seconds in extended trades, his Roar of the Slayer shreds your max HP scaling before it matters, and his level 6 Unstoppable Onslaught is a cross-map threat that punishes any forward positioning. Your level 6 Demonic Ascension does give you drain sustain, but Sion's passive zombie state means killing him is a two-phase commitment — you drain him down, he dies and keeps attacking, and if your R expires mid-zombie you take free damage. Play this window to accumulate fragments safely via W pokes at distance and avoid all-ins that don't start with a clean E-root landing.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are Sion's clearest ownership window and you have to survive them, not win them. Soul Furnace comes back every 15s at rank 1, Roar of the Slayer slows and shreds armour from 800 — it does nothing to your magic damage, but it holds you still for the charged Q — and Unstoppable Onslaught at 6 is a cross-map threat that punishes any forward positioning. Your Demonic Ascension does give drain sustain, but Glory in Death makes killing him a two-phase commitment: you drain him down, he reanimates with rapid attacks that heal him and scale off your maximum health, and if your R expires mid-zombie you take that for free. Buy Grievous Wounds before that fight, stack fragments with W at distance, and hold Flash for his R wall.

notes: NO chart edits, deliberately. The packet calls the chart a defect because Sion holds 5 of 7 stages at a 57.49% win rate, but this page already explains the gap honestly — Swain loses the 1v1 and wins the map — and every Sion row has a real argument in the adjacent whys. Inventing a power shift to satisfy the ratio would be worse than the flagged defect. Also left alone, and flagged by the mirror audit too: content.late's claim that once Swain is airborne 'his R drain cannot save him'. Whether Sion's knockup actually interrupts the drain is not in Riot's text and I could not verify it, so I did not touch that sentence.
